clue.text: Unhappy about own performance? Not if wheels get replaced by hybrid

indicators.note: placed by, i.e. next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: a hybrid plant or animal is a cross between two kinds

indicators.note: the letters of the words not if wheels are moved into new places, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Advice about cycling: a rider who swaps their wheels for a hybrid bike has nothing to be annoyed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid' looks like a type of bicycle in the surface; it gives CROSS. 'get replaced' rearranges NOT IF WHEELS into WITHONESELF.
explanation.definitionFit: Being annoyed at your own showing is to be angry at yourself, idiomatically.

clue.text: Royal regalia item changing hands for a risible figure

indicators.note: the R (right hand) is swapped for an L (left hand)

parts.note: a crown is part of the royal regalia

explanation.surface: A piece of the crown jewels passes to a new owner and becomes laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' turns the R of CROWN, for right, into L, for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus funnyman is a figure people laugh at, hence a risible one.

clue.text: Had too much time to open rigged vote

indicators.note: the period of time goes inside, opening up the jumbled letters
a rigged vote has been tampered with, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An election official is accused of taking too long to open a fixed ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' makes OVTE; 'to open' signals the period going inside it, not a ballot being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate to excess means consumed more food than was needed.

clue.text: Having broken desk, theologian (in drink) to make quick getaway

indicators.note: the desk is broken up, so its letters are rearranged
the theologian's letters go inside the word for a drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A drunk divinity scholar smashes a desk and then flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes SKED, and 'in' puts the theologian inside the drink, giving ADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper or scram is to make a hurried getaway.

clue.text: Data processed as some people dance

definitions.meaning: facts that have been processed into a usable form

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: IN FORMATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Processed facts are knowledge; formation dancing is done by dancers in a set pattern.

clue.text: Laugh about gutless Trump getting in a stew

indicators.note: the laugh wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a hoot is a burst of laughter

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, leaving only the outer letters of trump

explanation.surface: People laugh at a cowardly Donald Trump who is getting flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' and 'about' do the work; 'getting in a stew' reads as an idiom for being agitated, but the stew is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lancashire hotpot is a dish of meat and potatoes baked slowly, a kind of casserole.

clue.text: Thrown across line as hymns are

indicators.note: the sung word lies across, i.e. around, the letter for line

parts.note: hymns are sung

explanation.surface: Something is hurled across a line, the way hymns are performed in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts L inside SUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Slung is a past participle meaning tossed or hurled.

clue.text: Gutted starfish — left fragment

indicators.note: with the insides removed, so only the outer letters of starfish are kept

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left

explanation.surface: A cleaned starfish has a remnant left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' leaves the outer letters of STARFISH, SH; RED is used for left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap or tiny piece of something.

clue.text: Not having heard of French article about some fighting

indicators.note: the French article goes around the other letters

parts.note: une is the French for a, an article
a, as in some or one
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece about a skirmish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the French word goes around the other pieces; 'article' suggests a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant of something means you have no knowledge or news of it.

clue.text: German group receiving award mostly try to travel extensively

indicators.note: the group takes in the following letters

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
OBE is the British honour Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: most of the word try, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A German team that has been honoured tries to tour the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts the award and the trimmed try inside the group; 'mostly' drops the last letter. OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam the world means to journey widely across many countries.

clue.text: See 1
Fuss around an essential component of life for a fighter

indicators.note: the fuss surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
RNA, ribonucleic acid, is essential to all living cells

explanation.surface: Commotion over something vital for a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the acid inside the fuss. The fighter is the Panavia combat jet, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tornado is a military combat aircraft flown by the RAF.

clue.text: In Germany, a large antelope

indicators.note: the letters are contained in the following words

explanation.surface: A big antelope found in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters inside GermaNY A LArge.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: Give more water to monster taking refuge in rotten tree

indicators.note: the monster hides inside the jumbled tree
a rotten tree has decayed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Hydra was the many-headed monster of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Watering a monster that is hiding in a decaying tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' makes RETE, and 'taking refuge in' puts the many-headed monster of Greek myth inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore fluid lost by drying out is to put moisture back.

clue.text: Gentleman from Wiesbaden said to need kitchen furniture stylist

indicators.note: the German word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Herr is German for Mr or gentleman, and Wiesbaden is a German city
a dresser is a cupboard with shelves for plates

explanation.surface: A German man needs kitchen furniture and a designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns HERR into the word that sounds like it, HAIR; a dresser is a kitchen sideboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair stylist is someone who cuts and styles hair in a salon.

clue.text: See 25
Give a jab turning into a clue

indicators.note: the letters of into a clue are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking a swipe at someone, turned into a crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges INTO A CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate is to give someone an injection, informally a jab.

clue.text: Picture new organ arriving soon

parts.note: a drawing is a picture
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A painting of a new church organ, due to arrive shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching means coming close, about to arrive.

clue.text: Relative's rage about wounding gibe

indicators.note: the letters of rage are turned about into a new order

parts.note: a taunt is a hurtful jeer

explanation.surface: A family member's fury over a hurtful remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RAGE into GREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a relation two generations up.

clue.text: Man with bow could be cheating

definitions.meaning: a violinist, holding a bow, is playing his instrument
engaged in fraud or dishonest dealing

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a man playing a violin is on the fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for being engaged in petty fraud, such as fiddling expenses.

clue.text: Military displays rubbish 10s with body missing

parts.note: tat is shoddy rubbish

indicators.note: the middle of the plural fighters is taken out, leaving the ends

parts.note: the answer to 10-across in the plural, fighter jets

explanation.surface: Army shows put on junk, with the main part absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with body missing' strips RNAD from the middle of TORNADOS, leaving TOOS. A tattoo is a military show such as the Edinburgh Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military pageant with music and marching.

clue.text: See 5
Get rope twisted by pupil

indicators.note: the letters of get rope are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A student gets a rope twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges GET ROPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone guided and trained by a mentor, a disciple.

clue.text: It's said complete article finishes off lunatic fringe

parts.note: utter means complete or total
an is an indefinite article

indicators.note: the final letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: It is said that a whole newspaper piece wraps up the extremist fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' takes the last letters of lunatiC and fringE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken remark is something that has been voiced, a statement.

clue.text: Sheep eating nothing small wanders

indicators.note: the sheep takes in the letter for nothing

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sheep wanders about without eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts O inside RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to move about without a fixed destination.

clue.text: Turkey possibly caught fish

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
a batsman caught in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A turkey, perhaps, catches a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an abbreviation of a country; Turkey is the nation, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Teacher getting 22 wrong

indicators.note: the letters of the fish go wrong, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 22-across, a fish

explanation.surface: A teacher gets the answer to clue 22 wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of 22-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A private instructor teaches individual pupils or small groups.

clue.text: Fruit essential to save delivery service

indicators.note: the essential, central letters of save

parts.note: Ocado is a British online grocery delivery company

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is vital to rescuing a home delivery company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential to' takes the middle of sAVe; OCADO is a British online grocer that delivers to homes.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped green fruit used in guacamole.

clue.text: Workplace where skates are useless

definitions.meaning: a place where clerical work is done
away from the frozen surface skaters glide on

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into OFF ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's premises where staff sit at desks; skating needs a frozen rink.

clue.text: See 28
Removing odd parts of degaussers makes things simpler

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Getting rid of parts of demagnetisers makes life easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing odd parts of' keeps the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of dEgAuSsErS. A degausser demagnetises, as once used on CRT televisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To simplify or relieve something is to make it less difficult.

clue.text: Eats trendy fruits which could be fresher

indicators.note: the letters of eats trendy fruits could become another phrase when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats fashionable fruit that might be less stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which could be' rearranges EATS TRENDY FRUITS. 'Fresher' looks like a comparative adjective for fruit; it is British slang for a new undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a fresher is a university newcomer in the opening term of a course.
